lines.en: Someone makes it back while another struggles to find her place.
Not just in the forest, but in a world that has been tossing and turning in an attempt to throw her off since the moment she set foot somewhere she wasn’t meant to be.
Right now, she’s in another location just like that. And she has been dropped there by an entity that you may think you are familiar with when, in all actuality, you barely even know it.
If you think you know what I’m talking about, you’re wrong. Because each subject in each section of each sentence I speak to you is the opposite of what you want it to be.
Is that a riddle? Maybe.
Will it be on a quiz? Maybe.
Do I even want you to know?
Yes.
Because while it may often seem that divine intervention is not as much divine as it is simply intervening, the truth to all of this is that it’s really quite simple.
This is a love story.
And yes, there’s a lot more to it.
And yes, love itself is a complicated thing.
And yes, I’m only stalling right now because I’m desperate for someone to crawl further into the woods and every single second between what happens then and what happens now is keeping me safe.
But it’s putting everyone else in danger.
This world is a beautiful place.
And for every wire branching out from my heart, there is a wish that we’ll all come to understand that some day.
I word it differently every time, but I always mean the same thing.
It’s like rearranging a prayer at night because you think you might be able to trick God into giving you what you want through the clever twisting of letters.
Tonight, more letters will be twisted.
At my bedside and yours.
Or perhaps a bonfire full of familiar faces that will all experience hardship in the years to come if the years themselves are not the hardship in question.
This is a love story.
It’s a million love stories.
It’s a trillion love stories.
There is love everywhere we look- but we’re so desperate for enlightenment that we always try to turn it into something else.
We can’t sit still.
We have to move forward.
And if our legs will not cooperate, we have no other choice but to break them.
Right now, a girl is lost in the woods.
And while there are a million other things she should be worrying about-
While there are a trillion other things she should be worrying about-
What she wants is all too simple.
What she wants is her mother.
: Oh my God, no way. Did she really?
: Yeah. Kirin ain’t always been the best at stuff like that.
But her prayers are far too common.
She never learned to twist them.
: Hey. Is the gravure thingy over already?
: Oh, Ami! Took ya long enough. Just where the heck did ya drop Ayane off? Hiroshima?
: I took her exactly where I was supposed to. It’s not my fault it was like a bajillion miles away.
: Contest is over, Ami. But if you were worried about Uta and me getting too risque, you can find peace in the fact that Sensei’s bodyguards and Miss Watabe prevented us from getting too close.
: I didn’t expect you guys to do that. And it wouldn’t be my place to stop you either way.
: Wait, what?
: Who are you and what have you done with Ami?!
: Ah! The number one spot is starting to slip away! I have to update my journal!
: Did...something happen?
: Why is everybody being so weird?
: You’re the one who’s bein’ weird! This is the part where you’re supposed to be all “Ahhhh! Sensei is my uncle and we’re gonna move to Alabama” or somethin’!
: Is that really how you guys look at me?
: Isn’t that...how you want us to look at you?
: Yeah! The whole time I’ve known you, it’s been “Sensei this. Sensei that.” Did you drop your incest fetish in the woods or something?
: Yeah, this is weird...It’s like normal Ami went into the woods and then...Ami 2 came out of it or something.
: I promise I’m the same Ami as always. The only thing that changed is that I’m a little worried about Ayane right now...
: Hello?...Yasu?...Anyone?...
: I really hope she’s able to find her way back...that forest is pretty scary in the middle of the night.
: I’m sure she’ll be fine. If anything, we should be worried about Yasu. That girl can’t even find her way to the classroom most of the time.
: Yeah, and Touka’s been worried sick ever since she came back. Which, by the way, was way earlier than you, Ami. You sure you brought Ayane to the right place?
: Hello?....Anyone?...
: Yeah, definitely.
: But, Ayane stuff aside...I think I owe you an apology, Chika.
: You...do?
: Yeah...I was really rude when you came to the maid cafe the other day, and I wanted to let you know I didn’t mean anything bad by it.
: I’m just...not really good with change sometimes. But that’s not your fault, it’s mine. And I’m trying to get better when it comes to stuff like that.
: That’s...
: That’s really cool of you, Ami...Thank you.
: Doooooooes this mean you’ll come work at the cafe now? Because I can make that happen, Chika. I’m like the Yakuza boss of all things cute.
: Give me a night or two to sleep on it. There’s a huge sale on swimwear next week and, at the bare minimum, I’ll have to put in my two weeks notice. I can’t bail right before things get busy.
: Ahh...beautiful. This is the exact level of consideration and loyalty I look for in team members.
: Right after how cute they are in the uniform, of course.
: Are you...really trying to change, Ami?
: Yeah. Why do you ask?
: No...particular reason, I guess. I think it’s great that you’re going to give Sensei a little more breathing room.
: I just...I’m not really sure if, like...I understand how you’re trying to change. And whether or not you’re even serious about it.
: I don’t blame you for doubting me, Noriko...I just got a bit of a wake-up call the other day when Sensei told me that I’ve been suffocating him. That wasn’t ever my intention.
: He...told you that?
: Yeah...I’m a little ashamed to admit it, though...
: This whole time, I thought I was protecting him.
: After...
: After the...a...accident...I...
: I kind of...
: Well, I guess I’ve...never really been the same since then. And Sensei’s all I have now, so...
: Sensei or no Sensei...you’re not alone, Ami.
: Miku?
: That’s...all I wanted to say.
: I ain’t gonna be able to get the rest out.
: Miku’s right. And if you ever need anybody to talk to about any of that stuff, I’m sure all of us would be happy to help.
: You really mean that?...
: Yeah. Right, girls?
: Heck yeah! As the self-proclaimed Yakuza boss of cute stuff, you can count on Uta-chan to have her girls’ backs! Just make sure you keep showing up to work if you wanna keep that benefit.
: And I’ll...
: I’ll...be there for you too. Yeah.
: This...this is a trauma thing. I get it. It’s not your fault.
: Thank you, Noriko...
: Do you...
: Do you still look at me as...an honorary Nakayama sister?...
: Yeah...
: And I’ll...I’ll help you with...
: With anything you need...
: That means the world to me...
: Thank you.
: I’ve got your back too, Ami. And I’m looking forward to whatever version of you is able to exist without keeping Sensei on an invisible leash.
: I wouldn’t mind being kept on a leash if Sensei was the one who held it.
: Hey. You can at least have the courtesy of-
: Amen. Tie me up and keep me in a cage.
: Hey! I said I’m trying to change! Not that I’m already done changing!
: I, Uta Ushibori, hereby declare that I am in favor of the leash as well! Court adjourned!
: Come on, you guys! You’re making it hard on purpose!
And so the fire burns out and the night comes to an end...
A few new bonds are formed and everything ends happily ever after.
Ami gives up on pursuing a romantic relationship with her uncle.
Chika gets a job at the maid cafe and winds up earning enough money to take her sister somewhere nicer.
Uta and Miku improve their grades and somehow wind up at the top of the class.
And Noriko accepts that she will never be her sister...before stealing her man and marrying him.
Everything works out in the end.
Except it doesn’t.
You see, for every person living their best life, there are ten living their worst.
And if it ever feels like you’re lost in the woods with nowhere to go-
Well, you might actually be lost in the woods with nowhere to go.
: Yasu?! Are you out here?! You are, right?!
You might be stuck there forever.
: Let’s go back together! I’ll give you the point and everything! I just want to go home!
You might starve to death or be mauled by bears or some other equally devastating scenario because, while “love” may be in abundance, so is danger.
So is fear.
So are a million other negative emotions that we’re supposed to stave off in pursuit of three or four positive ones.
When things work out, life is amazing.
But when they don’t?
: Can anyone hear me?! Anyone at all?!
IT IS HELL
: Yasu! Please! I know you’re out here! Just follow the sound of my-
: Ya-
: Now, what’s a beautiful girl like you doing wandering around the woods in the middle of the night?
: Who...
: It must have been scary, huh? Being all alone out here.
: Do I...
: Do I know you from somewhere?...
: I don’t know. Do you?
: You just...
: I feel...
: I’m sure you feel a lot of things. It’s hard not to with so much chaos biting at your ankles.
: But things will get better. I just know it.
: How...
: How do you know that?...
: I just do, okay? Are you really going to question a mysterious girl who shows up in the woods right when you need her to?
: It just...
: It feels like this is all just a dream...
: I sure hope not! Something like that would completely devalue both of our existences.
: Hahah...hah...good point...
: I’m Ayane...it’s nice to meet you. If this even is our first meeting.
: I kind of like the idea of a first meeting in the woods. Sounds like something out of a fairytale.
: It feels like something out of a fairytale. I was beginning to think I’d be lost out here forever.
: Hey, who knows? Without my help, you might have been.
: You mean...you’ll help me find my way back?
: Of course! That’s my job, after all. I’m like a cute, mysterious tour guide.
: Does this cute, mysterious tour guide have a name?
: She does. And a rather nice one at that.
: Well, are you going to tell me? Or are you just going to keep being all mysterious?
: It’s easier to be mysterious when you don’t know what to call me.
: But I’m sure you’ll figure it out some day.
: And if you don’t, I am mega screwed.
: Then, mysterious tour guide girl...
: Yes, not-so-mysterious and stunningly beautiful blonde girl?
: Can I trust you when you say things are going to get better?
: Yes.
: You’re 100%% sure?
: I’m 110%% sure.
: But keep in mind, that doesn’t mean they won’t be hard.
: That thing you’re worrying about, though? With your friend who might actually be a serial killer or whatever?
: How do you-
: Don’t.
: She won’t lay a finger on you.
: What do you mean she...won’t lay a finger on me?
: Do you trust me or not? Cause if I were you, I’d take the whole “reading your mind” thing as a pretty big hint that it’s probably okay to trust me.
: Is that how you knew about that? You can read my mind?
: Maybe.
: Or maybe I just already knew?
: Or maybe you told me?
: That’s the beauty in being mysterious. I can say whatever I want to you and you’ll just have to nod and go along with it.
: She really won’t hurt me?...
: She really won’t hurt you.
: Is this the part where I just blindly entrust my future to a girl I met in the woods?
: So long as I can entrust mine to you one day.
: Now, come on! We’ve got a heck of a lot of walking to do!
: R-Right! Yeah!
: Adventure..........begin!
: H-Hey! You don’t have to pull so hard!
When the night comes to an end, just know-
I’ll be beside you always.
Through rain and fog, in heat and snow-
At the end of every hallway.
O’er these dark, unventured hills we climb-
With canisters of light.
The dawning of a new day dies.
And it’s here we say goodnight.
She found her.
